caption:
Too often, we treat the energy transition as something to be managed cautiously - especially when it comes to the role of young people. 
 
But the reality in the Global South tells a different story. In 2024, clean energy investments in electricity outpaced fossil fuels 7 to 1. This is not incremental progress; it’s a paradigm shift - one that youth are already helping to shape. 
 
As we accelerate into a future of electric vehicles, AI-integrated energy systems and smarter grids, we must reimagine, not just replicate, the systems we’ve inherited:

🔹 AI isn’t a silver bullet - its promise must not distract from the 1.18 billion people still living in energy poverty.
 🔹 EVs are only transformative if the benefits are shared - especially with communities in Africa, which holds over 50% of the world’s cobalt and manganese, yet often sees little value-added return.
 🔹 Energy is already central to climate action - cities use 78% of global energy and produce over 60% of emissions. The question isn’t whether to negotiate about energy, but how to ensure all voices are at the table.

Every day we should be working towards a sustainable energy revolution that addresses the needs and asks of people themselves. Young people are not simply  participants in this transition: they are already the dreamers, doers, and disruptors driving it forward.

Let’s leap forward: not cautiously, but courageously.
